summary: No single open table gives raw growth rate at declared temperatures across many species. Add-my-Pet holds a fitted Arrhenius temperature for 7,451 animal species entries (a derived parameter, interval not declared); BioNumbers has a handful of published Q10 values; two Dryad compilations (dryad.87v26 growth vs development thermal responses, 2011; dryad.56s5d84 rates across life's domains, 2018) and many single-taxon thermal-performance deposits hold rate-by-temperature data from which Q10 over a declared sub-optimal interval can be computed.
next_step: Download dryad.56s5d84 and dryad.87v26, filter rows to growth/development rates below the optimum, and declare the 10 °C intervals before computing; use AmP T_A as a secondary, derived comparison.
obstacles_confirmed: Relevant experiments require compilation from many deposits.
Fitted temperature parameters (AmP T_A) are not the same object as a raw rate ratio, and tabulated Q10 values (BioNumbers) are a sparse sample.
